title: Command and daemon can disagree on the socket when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR differs
description: The socket lives under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR when it is set, else in the state folder. A command run without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (cron, some ssh logins) looks for a different socket than the service's daemon, decides dibs isn't running, and fails to start it. Found while installing for real.
acceptance_criteria: Without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, dibs uses /run/user/UID when that folder exists and is ours (as systemd does), so both sides agree. Covered by a test.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10: socket falls back to /run/user/UID; tests isolated from the real runtime folder

title: dibs setup --undo --no-service still turns lingering off
description: undo(service=False) turns lingering off and deletes setup.json, forgetting that a service was installed, although --no-service asked to leave the service alone.
acceptance_criteria: With --no-service, undo leaves the service, lingering and their record in place; a later full undo still removes them. Covered by a test.

title: Two dibs instances of one user stop each other's GPU jobs
description: Each dibs (for example one with DIBS_HOME set and the default one) treats the other's job processes as outside dibs, so each guard stops the other's GPU jobs.
acceptance_criteria: A GPU process belonging to another dibs instance's job (DIBS_INSTANCE and DIBS_JOB_ID in its environment, instance not ours) is left alone and listed as another dibs's job. Covered by a test.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #12: GPU processes of another dibs instance's jobs are left alone

title: A crash while launching a job can mark a live job lost
description: schedule() writes a job as running before launch() returns the launcher's pid. If the daemon dies in those milliseconds, recover() finds a running job with no launcher pid and marks it lost: its reservation is freed and the guard may stop its GPU processes while the job runs on.
acceptance_criteria: recover() adopts a running job whose launcher pid was never recorded if its launcher is alive (found by the job folder in the launcher's command line), and only marks it lost when no launcher exists. Covered by a test.

title: A version clash between two dibs installs ends in a vague error
description: When the systemd service runs a different dibs build than the command (for example a uv tool install of one version and 'uv run' in a checkout of another), the CLI sees build_mismatch, restarts the daemon, the service brings back the same other build, and the retry fails with 'the dibs daemon refused', naming neither build.
acceptance_criteria: When the restart doesn't fix the mismatch, the error names both builds and says how to line them up (reinstall, or run the dibs that matches the service). Covered by a test.

title: Listing finished jobs decodes every stored environment
description: dibs queue --all and the hourly cleanup load every finished job's full JSON, including the submitter's environment, just to filter on when it ended.
acceptance_criteria: Finding recently finished jobs and jobs old enough to delete filters on an ended column in SQL, without decoding environments. Covered by a test; existing databases keep working.

title: Relative PATH entries are checked from the daemon's folder
description: When a job is submitted, the check that its command exists resolves relative PATH entries (., bin) against the daemon's working folder instead of the job's, so a command found through a relative PATH entry is wrongly rejected (or wrongly accepted).
acceptance_criteria: The command check resolves relative PATH entries against the job's working folder. Covered by a test.

title: The guard can miss children forked at the moment it stops a process
description: stop_with_message looks again for children after killing, but children of a killed process have already been re-parented by then, so a child forked at the last moment can escape.
acceptance_criteria: Children that exist at kill time are stopped even if their parent dies first. Covered by a test.
